label: Aristotle, Physics VII.1, 242b23-27: What primarily moves something in local, bodily motion…
interpretation: Typed reading: whatever primarily moves something in local, bodily motion touches it or is continuous with it (242b24-26: εἰ τὸ κινοῦν πρώτως κατὰ τόπον καὶ σωματικὴν κίνησιν ἀνάγκη ἢ ἅπτεσθαι ἢ συνεχὲς εἶναι τῷ κινουμένῳ, καθάπερ ὁρῶμεν ἐπὶ πάντων). Restricted to primary movers and local motion, as the sentence is; the -A reading has only two atoms and no mover or moved. The sentence is a conditional ('if …'); Aristotle asserts its antecedent by appeal to what we see in all cases, and the reading records that assertion.
